role: Cover illustration; imaginative reconstruction, not archaeological evidence
prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create a wide 16:9 editorial museum illustration for the cover of an educational HTML slide deck about Indus inscriptions. Subject: a possible Bronze Age Indus urban workshop and goods exchange, c.2600–1900 BCE, understood as an imaginative reconstruction, not an excavated scene. Quiet warm clay and sandstone palette, muted teal shadows, fine ink-and-watercolor texture, elegant serious archaeology book illustration. Composition: strong scene on the RIGHT two thirds: close view of a person's brown hands pressing a small square seal into damp clay on a tied bundle; terracotta storage jars and simple balance weights nearby; sunlit fired-brick walls and modest workshop courtyard behind. No exact deciphered writing and no invented legible text. Any seal face too small to read, simple animal silhouette and tiny abstract marks, no Sanskrit, no hieroglyphs. LEFT third mostly pale textured empty space for an HTML title added later. No titles, labels, lettering, modern objects, kings, temples or fantasy. Wide composed artwork, not a photograph, highly readable forms. Suitable for a refined archaeology learning presentation.
review: Inspected the generated image. The final cover labels the scene and all depicted objects and signs as illustrative.
